fit: liquid tart cherry concentrate and pretraining fatigue in healthy athletes
assessment: Table 6.3 reports week-four fatigue 2.5 versus 3.1 with different week-one levels. The thesis describes no clear group difference and supplies no fatigue p value or confidence interval. Dried fruit and Parkinson fatigue were outside this trial.

fit: tart cherry and cocoa mixture with unresolved exertion comparison
assessment: The abstract describes a randomized athlete trial. The Methods describe laboratory formulations and sensory panel work. Table 3 lists ungrouped before and after RPE values without an identified comparator or verified trial allocation.

fit: mixed seed extract and rat locomotor activity
assessment: Figures 1 and 2 report less catalepsy and higher activity with a mixture of almond, peanut and watermelon seed extracts. No arm tested watermelon alone or raw flesh. Animal locomotion differs from measured bradykinesia in patients.

fit: acute drooling during suspected seed allergy in a child
assessment: The author preprint reports excess drooling during an acute allergic reaction to a mixed snack containing watermelon seed paste. Previous flesh was tolerated and the suspected culprit lacks challenge confirmation. The clinical context and preparation do not establish a Parkinson symptom effect.

fit: freeze-dried commercial cranberry juice applied to a cell-free MAO-A assay
assessment: The article reports inhibition with discordant IC50 values and units. The enzyme source is unspecified. No participant exposure or depression outcome was tested. A separate human adipose experiment by overlapping authors used pomegranate.

fit: incidental watermelon mention and orthostatic blood pressure in a dementia case
assessment: The original letter reports 130/84 mmHg supine and 114/79 mmHg standing during medication review in a posterior cortical atrophy case. The watermelon episode illustrates a visual error. The report gives no ingestion time or change in lightheadedness after a food intervention.
